intent: A small icon button at the trailing end of one menu row, acting on that row's item.
typical_uses: A "more" button opening the row's own menu of commands

dont_use_when.situation: An action on a whole section

invariants.text: The action is a 20px square absolutely positioned 4px from the item's right edge and vertically centred on the row, sizing a direct `svg` child to the small icon size; collapsed to the icon rail it is not displayed.

With `showOnHover` the action is transparent until its item is hovered or holds focus, or until the action has `aria-expanded="true"` or `data-popup-open`; it stays in the tab order while transparent.
It renders a native button with no accessible name of its own; an icon-only action needs `aria-label`.

rtl.by: sidebar.module.css positions .menuAction with the physical `right` property, so it stays on the right edge under a right-to-left direction

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's useRender takes an element or a function of the action's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the action becomes a menu trigger.

good.title: A named action revealed on hover

bad.title: The action nested in the row's button
bad.why: A button inside a button is invalid markup and joins the action to the row's accessible name; the action is the button's sibling inside SidebarMenuItem.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's useRender takes an element or a function of the action's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the action becomes a menu trigger.
